scores.rationale: Several snippets bear on whether organismal chemical/elemental composition varies with nutritional status. Multiple snippets support the fact: [15] directly shows starvation creates nutrient deficits altering macronutrient selection; [16]/[17] show feeding and starvation gradients change isotopic budgets; [7] shows biochemical composition (protein, lipid, carbohydrate) varies with trophic conditions; [12] shows protist stoichiometry varies under resource conditions; [9], [13], and [18] document intraspecific stoichiometric variation partly driven by diet/resource availability. The notable counterpoint is [4], which reports homeostatic maintenance of constant cell composition during prolonged darkness/starvation in a cyanobacterium, and several stoichiometry papers emphasize homeostasis ([2], [3]). However, the latter generally describe constrained (bounded) variation rather than no variation, and the bulk of relevant evidence affirms that nutritional status affects composition. Many snippets are merely topical (nutrition or stoichiometry generalities). Overall the corpus moderately and predominantly corroborates the stylized fact, with one partial contradiction reflecting taxon- and metric-dependent homeostasis.

snippets.text: ABSTRACT The chemical composition of organisms in relation to their environmental resource availability is an area of intense research activity. We studied the changes in cell composition of the cyanobacterium Phormidium autumnale in response to prolonged darkness. Cells allocated their internal resources in a homeostatic manner, oxidizing all the three major cellular constituents in a proportional way. This resulted in constant C/N and carbohydrates, lipids and proteins ratios that remained unaltered throughout the whole incubation period. We propose the maintenance of balanced cell composition (homeostasis) as an evolutionary strategy related to environmental transitory changes.
